entries.id: clause 6 v2 (face qualifier and seam pair on every warrant)

verbatim.face_qualifier_mandatory_on_warrants: WARRANT-onset, WARRANT-close and WARRANT-rival carry a face qualifier: ':near' (the seam verse inside the unit the seam bounds — the row's first verse for its onset, its last verse for its close, the candidate onset verse for a rival), ':far' (the adjacent verse across the seam), ':interior' (an in-span verse the warrant rests on that is neither — e.g. the מופת partner at 24:24 for the 24:27 close; permitted for WARRANT-close and WARRANT-onset only when the annotation names the device). Form: 'oshb:Ezek.33.20 [WARRANT-onset:far] pe-marked close behind the dateline'. For WARRANT-onset and WARRANT-close the member DERIVES the face from (verse, span) and FAILS LOUD on a mismatch, so the qualifier is verified, not free text. For WARRANT-rival the seam is not in the schema, so the annotation's first token names the seam pair — 'oshb:Ezek.33.12 [WARRANT-rival:near] 33.11/33.12 ve'attah, same audience, unlicensed' — and the member checks the ref's verse is one side of the pair and the qualifier matches that side.
verbatim.absence_tokens: WARRANT-absence (a single verse or a range; the boundary rests on the absence — 'no formula, mark, K/Q or paseq at C:V' or 'inside C:V-C:V') and DISCLOSURE-absence (a single verse or a range; recorded, the boundary does not rest on it — the honest home for 'device census records no stroke here'). WARRANT-absence-over-range is retained as a deprecated alias the member accepts and maps to WARRANT-absence. The citation sweep's mark, paseq and puncta arms treat any *-absence token as a NEGATED claim and verify the census is EMPTY at the verse(s): a false absence (device present) is a defect (Q6.2).
verbatim.worked_example_per_token: the author brief carries one worked example per token, including the three cases lane 01 found divergent: a verse with neither device nor mark that the rationale rests on (WARRANT with :near/:far, the ground named — content is a warrant when the rationale rests on it); an inventoried device the boundary does not rest on (DISCLOSURE-device, never ANCHOR); a device that is not recorded (never DISCLOSURE-device; ANCHOR or *-absence).
verbatim.face_of_the_evidence: X2 (lane 02): an MT-borne device (mark, paseq, K/Q, note, formula membership) is cited on the oshb: face; a WEB quotation on the web: face; inside the ch 20/21 zone every entry is dual as already ruled. Outside the zone this is a deterministic re-face (identity numbering) and runs as a MECHANICAL sweep with a distinct check; the two rows lane 02 names as inverting near/far in prose (P11-001, P11-013) are in the prose pass.
verbatim.retro_qualification: The 'existing entries are NOT re-tokenised' clause is amended for ONE deterministic case: every WARRANT-onset and WARRANT-close token this wave installed receives its derived face qualifier by a mechanical sweep (derivable from verse and span; adds information; changes no claim), distinct-checked. WARRANT-rival tokens receive the qualifier and seam pair in the author repair batch (author work: the seam must be read off the SRA). Pre-wave descriptive entries are still not re-tokenised.
verbatim.why_a_qualifier_and_not_a_split_token: a split (WARRANT-onset-near / WARRANT-onset-far) doubles the vocabulary and still leaves the rival unsaid; a qualifier the member verifies is smaller and auditable.

verbatim.question: Which grammar gives every forward-merge WARRANT-rival a verified face (17 entries + S4-085's qualifier part, which is the same P08-003 entry S4-060 names + S4-010's shared-onset variant)?
verbatim.why_neither_reading_as_offered: Reading A puts :near on the first absorbed verse; own_seam_faces makes that same verse the FAR face of the row's own close seam, so one verse would carry both polarities and the member could not verify it. Reading B (b) re-anchors the entry to the merged unit's onset, which for a forward merge is the row's own onset (the P01-013 coincidence) and which the audit view reads as OUTSIDE_THE_SPAN — a token that adds nothing the calibration can use. Both readings force a merge into a grammar written for interior candidate onsets.
verbatim.ruling_the_merge_qualifier: Clause 6 v2 gains a fourth face-qualifier value for WARRANT-rival only: ':merge'. A merge-shaped rival (the rejected alternative dissolves one of the row's OWN seams and proposes no interior seam) is written 'PREFIX:REF [WARRANT-rival:merge] C.V/C.V+1 GLOSS' where the pair is the row's own seam the merge would dissolve — its close seam (last/last+1) for a forward merge, its onset seam (first-1/first) for a backward merge — and REF is the absorbed material: for a forward merge REF's FIRST verse is the pair's second member (last+1); for a backward merge REF's LAST verse is the pair's first member (first-1). REF may be the first absorbed verse alone. A merge token carries NO :near/:far polarity, because the faces of the contested seam are the row's own faces and are already tokenised by WARRANT-onset/close:near/far; the merge token records that the seam is contested and which alternative contests it. A two-sided (whole-unit) merge is written as one merge token per dissolved own seam, each REF the absorbed range on that side. The face-of-the-evidence rule applies to the prefix as for any entry (content gloss -> web:; an MT device or absence named in the gloss -> oshb:; dual inside the zone).
verbatim.why_this_and_not_a_split_token: one qualifier value, one member arm, deterministic from (span, pair, ref) alone; it reaches every entry the census found (17 unqualified forward, 11 backward already mis-paired, 1 shared-onset) with the same rule, and it lets the CONF-CAL member say 'contests own close seam' instead of 'unpaired' or 'outside the span'.
verbatim.entry_orders: one exact before/after per entry, in orders_for_final_remediation (source_item S4-009…S4-078, S4-010, S4-085); all mechanical except P03-007 (gloss and face change) and P10-015's 44.1 single-verse entry (re-tokened as the row's close far face because it states a fact about the seam's far face, not a rival)
verbatim.member_arm: see tool_orders[0]; the role_tokens member's phase flips to post only under role_tokens_phase_flip.condition

verbatim.ruling: NOT a licensed onset. The לכן-turn messenger formula with no addressee change and no verse-final close-role formula before it is an onset-class device (a messenger formula) that CUT-RULE does not license: it is the discourse turn from indictment to verdict inside one speech, which is what לכן does in Ezekiel's prose. The 'licensed as a discourse frame' category #e13 used at 17:19 does not exist; #e15 already withdrew it. A mark on the verse before corroborates the paragraph and licenses nothing. Addressee readings: 17:19 none (third-person king throughout 17:12-21); 20:30 none (house of Israel already the named audience at 20:27, and a title shift inside one audience group is not an addressee change — the P08-002 precedent); 39:25 none (same hearers as 39:21-24). Tier: the bytes MEASURED; the addressee findings are READINGS on measured bytes, stated as such.
verbatim.consequence_for_the_scale: As a row's OWN onset near face this shape is the MEDIUM_LOW limb exactly as #e15 wrote it ('an own seam whose near face carries an onset-class device that is not licensed … whatever its far face carries'). As the FAR face of the preceding row's close seam it carries NO signal (a close far face carries a signal only when it carries a licensed onset or a scene change). As a RIVAL near face it is unlicensed; the rival is paragraph-grade unless its far face ends on a close-role signal, in which case it is two-faced-unlicensed and bars HIGH.

Predicate for the member: the consonantal skeleton ויאמר אלי, ויאמר יהוה אלי or וידבר אלי at the verse's head, in a verse inside a vision stretch. Vision stretches (frames MEASURED: hand-of-YHWH / transport openers and the return clauses; extents INFERRED from the frames, stated so): 1:1-3:15; 3:22-3:27; 8:1-11:25; 37:1-14; 40:1-48:35. entries.id: the scale's application rules for this book

verbatim.R-1_lakhen_turn: as c3: unlicensed onset-class device; MEDIUM_LOW on an own near face; no signal on a far face; paragraph-grade or two-faced-unlicensed as a rival.
verbatim.R-2_reader_found_signals: A verse-final refrain, inclusio, thesis restatement, execution report, naming summary, outcry, aetiological note, list heading or any other close or turn the census does not list is, for the scale, 'a discourse turn without formula': it sustains MEDIUM_LOW on an own near face and carries NO signal on a far face. It is disclosed in the row as the reading it is, and it separates MEDIUM_LOW from LOW. Two signals from #e15's own close-role list are exceptions and license a near face: (a) a GENRE COLOPHON in the composition's own voice — 19:14 קִינָ֥ה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה and 43:12 זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת; NOT the reported taunt of MT 21:5 (= WEB 20:49), which is the prophet's outcry; (b) a VISION RETURN — the return movement's completion verse: 3:15 (arrival at Tel-abib after the transport of 3:12-14) and 11:25 (the report-back completing the return clause of 11:24). Recognition-shaped clauses outside the inventory (20:26 אשר-form; 2:5 and 33:33 'a prophet has been among them') are NOT counted: the inventory governs membership (C2-amended); they are routed to the inventory's next version (tool_orders[2]). The Tyre refrain (26:21, 27:36, 28:19) and the other measured-distribution refrains are recorded for method section 17 as candidates for a future 'unit-final-only refrain' class; not applied in Ezekiel.
verbatim.R-3_speech_introductions_outside_a_visio: ויאמר יהוה אלי / 'speak to' / 'say to' commands outside a vision are onset-class devices governed by the two CUT-RULE limbs like the messenger formula and ve'attah (23:36 is licensed under (a): the address turns from Oholibah to the prophet). A SCENE CHANGE is a far-face signal on a CLOSE seam only (own_seam_faces); on an onset far face the test is 'ends on a close-role signal'; on any near face a scene change without a device is a discourse turn (MEDIUM_LOW).
verbatim.R-4_dependent_completion: #e14 Q2's refinement applied as the readers applied it: verse-final in effect at 7:9, MT 21:10, 22:22, 25:17, 28:26, 33:29, 36:23, 37:28; mid-verse (independent clause follows) at 6:10, 16:43, 18:23 (as #e15 measured), 18:32, 29:9, 36:32. 6:10's second half has its own finite verb and no subordinator: independent by the letter.
verbatim.R-5_size_genre_and_section_7: CONF-CAL governs over the length posture: a whole-chapter or long span the strategy licenses is not held below its faces for size, and 'the cap disclosed' is a disclosure duty, not a grade ground (A7 sets no confidence rule by length; #e13 CONF-CAL excludes licensed size). A section-7-named held question is a ground (MEDIUM_LOW without bespoke rationale; the strategy's 'hold at medium_low/low' direction permits either with bespoke rationale). Where I cannot see the strategy (it is not a pinned input of this ruling) the order is CONDITIONAL: the orchestrator checks the pinned strategy's section 7 for the row's span or a region containing it and records the text checked; if named, KEEP with the section-7 ground written into the prose; if not named, MOVE as ordered.
verbatim.R-6_strategy_named_cut_sites: A verse the strategy names as a row-grade cut site or re-onset (36:33 and 36:37 per #e14's extract of section 7) is a LICENSED onset at that verse by the strategy's own rule (licensed_onset: 'an onset-class device that the strategy's rules make a row-grade onset AT THAT VERSE'). The CONF-CAL member takes the list of such sites as a data fixture extracted by the orchestrator from the pinned strategy with its digest.
verbatim.R-7_shared_seams: A shared seam has the same FACE FACTS from both rows (#e14's consistency rule restated for #e15's definitions); each row's GRADE follows its own near face, because a row's confidence records the evidence for its own edges. So P08-012 (close near 36:23 licensed, far 36:24 empty) is MEDIUM and P08-013 (onset near 36:24 empty) is MEDIUM_LOW on one seam; the six ch-18 rows are all MEDIUM_LOW because every near face is unlicensed.
verbatim.R-8_temple_survey: Inside the measuring survey 40:5-42:20 an object turn (a new measured object, a fronted noun, a sighting clause, a measuring verb, the steps notice) is NOT a discourse turn for the scale; only transport verses and 'he said to me' verses are. LOW stands on those faces; MEDIUM_LOW needs one of the two.
verbatim.R-9_two_verse_rows: A shipped row under three verses that is not a complete word-event unit (P06-013 28:25-26; P04-007 MT 21:11-12) is held at its current grade with the over-split guard disclosed, and its tiling is escalated (E3); the grade is not raised on faces the guard says should not have produced a row.
verbatim.R-10_register_and_schema_vocabulary: Schema enum values (unit_type values such as 'disputation_oracle', parent-collection labels 'P1'…'P11', grade tokens 'medium_low', 'high') are the record's internals and are BARRED in prose like a key path; state the substance ('the disputation-oracle category', 'the collection this row opens', 'held at reduced confidence because …'). Prose states the GROUND for a grade, never the enum word. Evidence-tier labels 'tier-1/3/4' are strategy scale labels and are BARRED for the same reason; the tier words OW-18 requires are the OW-18 words (measured, read, inferred) and the witness. 'single witness' unhyphenated is accepted where the gate accepts it; every MARK MENTION in a field carries the disclosure once per field, and a rewritten entry that names a mark carries it in the entry.
verbatim.R-11_pre_wave_descriptive_entries: The bar on re-tokenising pre-wave descriptive entries stands as the default. One ruled exception: where an ORDER on the row (a grade move's ground, a measured-false repair, a register order) makes a pre-wave entry's wording false, misleading or contradicted, the entry is rewritten under that order and the entry-form gate's tokenisation requirement is met. The re-tokenisations already made under such orders (P01-001, P01-013, P02-002, P02-005, P02-016, P05-002, P05-003, P05-008, P06-001, P08-010, P10-012) are RATIFIED: every token checked was true to its verse. S4-090 (P02-018 13:21/13:23) is granted under this exception because the grade move ordered here rests on 13:23's counted 2fp form.

verbatim.question: How far does R-6 (strategy-named cut sites license an onset) reach, now that lane A (A11) has read the pinned strategy and found the fixture wider than #e14's extract, and does a named site whose stated premise is byte-false still license?
verbatim.ruling: R-6 reaches every verse the pinned strategy names as a cut BY VERSE: section 6's internal-cut list (16:35, 23:22, 16:59; 20:27, 20:30, 20:39; the transports 40:17, 40:28, 40:32, 40:35, 40:48, 41:1, 42:1, 42:15), section 6's chapter-division sentence (46:1 messenger formula; 48:1 'these are the names'), section 7's 'Internal cuts at 16:35, 16:44, 16:59', and the 36:33/36:37 re-onsets already in R-6. A naming LICENSES the face only where the bytes carry the onset-class device the naming rests on; a naming whose premise a ruling has measured byte-false (20:27 and 20:30 per #e13 R8; 23:22's 'messenger formula with addressee change', the 2fs address standing already at 23:21) carries the seam as the plan's seam (a section-7 ground, MEDIUM_LOW) but licenses nothing; a naming that rests on no device at all (16:44, הִנֵּה֙ כָּל הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל is a proverb about the city, not a mashal command) likewise carries the seam and licenses nothing. A held question or a region is not a naming (c3's strategy_check_condition stands).

verbatim.question: R-4 lists MT 21:10 as 'verse-final in effect'; both lanes measure it mid-verse by R-4's own 6:10 test. Which?
verbatim.ruling: MID-VERSE. MEASURED: MT 21:10 reads וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב עֽוֹד — the recognition stands at the head, its content clause הוֹצֵ֥אתִי חַרְבִּ֖י follows, and then לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב עֽוֹד, a finite clause with no subordinator; R-4 called 6:10's לֹ֥א אֶל חִנָּ֤ם דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ independent by the letter on exactly that test. Parity requires the same reading here. verbatim.question: Does a section-7 naming block a low -> medium_low move (the orchestrator's literal reading of R-5, which BLOCKED P10-013, P01-001, P01-014, P02-006), when both blind lanes read section 7 as directing no low?

So a naming caps a row at medium_low (it blocks moves to medium or high, as the check applied to P08-015, P03-020 and the rest) but it does not hold a row at LOW: within a named region LOW stands only where the row's own text states a bespoke ground for LOW. P10-013 is re-resolved as MOVE (its prose grounds the row's existence — the inclusio — and the survey rule, not a ground for LOW). The three siblings the check blocked on the same reading (P01-001, P01-014, P02-006) were raised by no reviewer and are NOT re-reviewed here; they are routed to the orchestrator under T-3 for the same text check.

entries.verbatim: The schema has one strongest_rejected_alternative; it holds the strongest. Any further live interior candidate is disclosed in one clause of device_notes as weighed and not taken, with the device that would carry it named. No new field. Whether 13:14/13:15 is the strongest alternative for that row is the peer's call.

## 5. The A9/A16 weighing duty

Where a rival seam exists, the row must **weigh** it, not ignore it and not merely mention it. A weighing says:
what the rival's near face carries, what its far face carries, whether CUT-RULE licenses it, and on what stated
ground the row holds against it. A licensed two-faced rival held on stated grounds is **MEDIUM** — that is
CONF-CAL's second limb, and it is a normal, defensible outcome, not a weakness to hide.

A rival you cannot weigh honestly is an escalation, not a rewrite.

entries.id: CUT-RULE and the precedence of a driver over a mark
entries.verbatim:
## 1. CUT-RULE — the messenger and *ve'attah* second limb

The strategy states this rule three ways. **ONE formulation governs** (ruling #e13):

> A messenger formula is a **sub-onset** when
> **(a)** the addressee changes, **or**
> **(b)** the verse immediately before it **ENDS on** a close-role formula (utterance or recognition, any
> inventoried or D3 variant) — **VERSE-FINAL, not mid-verse**.
>
> **A mark alone never satisfies limb (b).** Strategy lines 322-323 are an incomplete summary, not a third rule.
>
> The same two limbs govern **"and you, son of man"** (*ve'attah*) inside an already-open unit: it is a sub-onset
> when the addressee changes or the unit has closed on a verse-final close-role formula before it. A **renewed
> command to the same addressee after a verse-final UTTERANCE signature is a paragraph**, not an onset.

**PRECEDENCE — a driver outranks a mark** (ruling #e13):

> A licensed text-signal driver (transport verb inside a vision, word-event, dateline, messenger/*ve'attah*
> sub-onset under CUT-RULE, refrain close) **outranks a closed-section boundary**, which is weak corroboration
> and is disclosed **for the alternative it corroborates**. The over-split guard — "a row under 3 verses only
> when it is a complete word-event unit" — then governs whether a licensed driver yields a row at all.

Note the direction in the second clause: a mark that supports the *rival* is disclosed as supporting the rival.
Do not write it up as if it supported the row.

entries.id: CONF-CAL (no grade is moved in this step)
entries.verbatim:
**CONF-CAL — what confidence measures** (binding, ruling #e13):

> Confidence records the strength of the **boundary evidence**, not the quality of the row's prose (which you are
> repairing), not size conformance where the strategy licenses the size, and not a genre hold the strategy
> licenses with disclosure.
>
> - **HIGH** — both seams two-faced (a licensed text signal on the near face and a text signal — onset, close or
>   scene change — on the far face) and no rival seam licensed under CUT-RULE. A mark-only or paragraph-grade
>   rival is weighed under A9/A16, **never fatal**.
> - **MEDIUM** — both seams carry a licensed near-face signal but one far face carries only a mark or nothing,
>   **OR** a two-faced rival is held on stated grounds.
> - **MEDIUM_LOW** — a seam whose near-face signal is itself weak (mid-verse formula; discourse turn without
>   formula) with an empty far face, or a region §7 holds without bespoke rationale.
> - **LOW** — a seam without a licensed text signal, or where the strategy directs low.
>
> §7's direction is the tie-breaker where it names the region. **No row's confidence is raised unasked.**
